params.title: Inspections, Installations, Instruments
params.subtitle: Installing GMDSS equipment correctly, the annual ship station inspection, and the test instruments a maintainer sets up and reads.

onScreen: Installation, the annual inspection and test instruments
scenes.narration: This lesson covers 3 parts of a GMDSS maintainer's job. GMDSS is the Global Maritime Distress and Safety System. First, installing equipment correctly. Second, carrying out and recording the annual GMDSS ship station inspection. Third, choosing, setting up and reading the test instruments you'll use. Let's start with installation, beginning with the Inmarsat-C terminal.

callouts.label: Ground: copper strap brazed to the steel terminal and steel hull
Wide strap: low impedance; brazing won't loosen; no aluminum on steel
Antenna: at least 8 meters from other Inmarsat antennas
After installation: enter your Inmarsat Mobile Number
Never send a distress alert as a test

onScreen: Copper strap brazed to the terminal and the steel hull
Low impedance, won't loosen, no galvanic corrosion
Antenna 8 meters from other Inmarsat antennas
Never send a distress alert as a test
scenes.narration: The best method for grounding an Inmarsat-C terminal is a copper strap brazed to the steel terminal and the ship's steel hull. A wide strap has low impedance, a brazed joint won't loosen like a bolted one, and aluminum on steel invites galvanic corrosion. When installing the Inmarsat-C antenna, the minimum distance to other Inmarsat antennas is 8 meters. After the system is fully installed, your Inmarsat Mobile Number must be entered in the terminal. And a distress alert must never be sent as a test.

params.title: Antennas, transducers and the compass
items: Full-duplex VHF: maximum separation between the transmitting and duplex receiver antennas
So the transmitter does not desensitize the receiver
Depth finder transducers: in an area not subject to cavitation
Air bubbles absorb and scatter the acoustic pulse
Bridge equipment separation: refers to the magnetic compass (compass safe distance)

onScreen: Keeps the receiver from being desensitized
Bubbles absorb and scatter the pulse
scenes.narration: 3 more installation rules. For a full-duplex VHF, or very high frequency, radiotelephone, the most important consideration is maximum separation between the transmitting antenna and the duplex receiver antenna, so the transmitter does not desensitize the receiver. For depth finder transducers, the most important factor is an area not subject to cavitation, because air bubbles absorb and scatter the acoustic pulse. And bridge equipment separation recommendations generally refer to the magnetic compass. That's the compass safe distance.

params.title: The annual GMDSS inspection
items: Requires a GMDSS Maintainer's License, not an operator's license
Battery test: off charge, at the maximum required load
Measure and record the maximum discharge current and voltage
Inmarsat-C: send a brief test message to your own terminal
That 1 message proves both transmit and receive

onScreen: Battery: off charge, maximum required load
Record maximum discharge current and voltage
Inmarsat-C: test message to your own terminal
scenes.narration: Every year, a GMDSS ship station gets an annual inspection. Conducting it requires a GMDSS Maintainer's License, not an operator's license. The battery test is made with the battery off charge and at the maximum required load. You measure and record the maximum discharge current and voltage. And the easiest way to test the Inmarsat-C terminal for proper operation is to send a brief test message to your own terminal. Getting it back proves both transmit and receive.

params.title: Annual VHF tests
rows: Operation from all required power sources

scenes.narration: The VHF radio has its own list of required annual tests. Measure the power output and the VSWR, the voltage standing wave ratio, on channels 6, 13 and 16. Check that the equipment is within frequency tolerance, and that it operates from all required power sources. Carrier deviation measurement is not a required annual VHF test. Remember the channels: 6, 13 and 16.

params.title: After the station passes the survey

onScreen: Log: technician and Master/owner both certify
Separate from the Radio Station License
scenes.narration: After the station passes the annual inspection, or survey, 2 things follow. First, the log entries must include certification by both the inspecting technician and the vessel's Master or owner that the inspection was successful. Both of them sign, not just 1. Second, the vessel is issued a Cargo Ship Safety Certificate. That certificate is separate from the Radio Station License, which is not the document the survey issues.

params.title: Meter tolerance: 5 V on the 6 volt scale

scenes.narration: Now test instruments, starting with the multimeter. Its tolerance is a percentage of the reading plus a fixed number of counts of the last digit. Take a 4 digit meter with an accuracy of 0.15 percent and 2 counts, set on the 6 volt scale, measuring a 5 volt DC, or direct current, source. On the 6 volt scale it resolves 0.001 volts, so 2 counts add 0.002 volts. The error is 0.0015 times 5 volts, which is 0.0075, plus 0.002, for 0.0095 volts. That's about 0.01 volts. So expect 4.99 to 5.01 volts DC.

params.title: For the exam: 24 volts on the 60 volt scale
items: On the 60 volt scale the meter resolves 0.01 V, so 2 counts add 0.02 V
For the exam, a 24 volt DC source reads 23.62 to 24.38 volts DC
That keyed window is 24 V ± 0.38 V
It matches 1.5% plus 2 counts (0.36 V + 0.02 V), not the 0.15% in the question

onScreen: For the exam: 23.62 to 24.38 volts DC
scenes.narration: Now the same meter, 0.15 percent and 2 counts, set on the 60 volt scale and measuring a 24 volt DC source. On the 60 volt scale the meter resolves 0.01 volts, so 2 counts add 0.02 volts. For the exam, the keyed answer is 23.62 to 24.38 volts DC. That's 24 volts, plus or minus 0.38 volts. Be aware that this window really matches 1.5 percent plus 2 counts, 0.36 plus 0.02 volts, not the 0.15 percent in the question. Choose 23.62 to 24.38 volts DC on the exam anyway.

params.title: A VHF signal generator: what matters most

blocks.label: RF signal generator
blocks.note: Most important spec: low signal leakage

blocks.label: Output attenuator
blocks.note: Good lab type: down to 0.1 µV

blocks.label: VHF receiver under test
blocks.note: Sees only what the attenuator indicates

onScreen: RF signal generator: low signal leakage
No leaked signal reaching the receiver
Receiver sees only the indicated signal
scenes.narration: For VHF measurements, the most important specification for an RF, or radio frequency, signal generator is low signal leakage. You set its output level with the attenuator, and a good lab type signal generator for VHF should be able to reduce its output to 0.1 microvolt. If signal leaked out around the attenuator, the receiver under test would pick up more than the setting shows. With low leakage, the receiver sees only the signal the attenuator setting indicates.

callouts.label: 10:1 attenuation probe: a load of about 10 MΩ shunted by 12 pF
A 9 MΩ probe resistor in series with the scope's 1 MΩ input
Dual-trace Mode control: either channel alone, or both channels combined
Input coupling and time base have their own separate controls

onScreen: 10:1 probe: about 10 megohms shunted by 12 pF
9 megohms in the probe plus the 1 megohm input
Mode: either channel alone or both combined
Coupling and time base: separate controls
scenes.narration: On the oscilloscope, a 10 to 1 attenuation probe presents a load of about 10 megohms shunted by 12 picofarads. That's a 9 megohm resistor in the probe, in series with the scope's 1 megohm input. On a dual-trace oscilloscope, the Mode control selects either channel alone, or a combination of both channels. Input coupling and the time base are set with their own controls, not with the Mode control.

params.title: Function generator and logic probe
items: Simple function generator: sine, square and triangular waves
Logic probe red LED: a high state
It can't identify a short: red and green LEDs on together don't indicate one

onScreen: A logic probe can't identify a short
scenes.narration: A simple function generator usually provides 3 kinds of signal: sine waves, square waves and triangular waves. Now the logic probe and its LEDs, or light emitting diodes. The red LED indicates a high state. The green LED indicates a low state. The amber LED indicates a pulse. A logic probe cannot identify a short, so the statement that both red and green LEDs on indicate a short is false.

blocks.label: Sharp 1000 Hz bandstop
blocks.note: Notch filter removes the test tone

onScreen: Sharp 1000 Hz bandstop filter removes the tone
SINAD in decibels; 12 dB is the usual reference
scenes.narration: SINAD is short for signal plus noise and distortion. A SINAD meter is a multi-range audio frequency voltmeter, calibrated in decibels, with a sharp internal 1000 hertz bandstop, or notch, filter. It first measures the total audio: signal plus noise plus distortion. Then the bandstop filter removes the 1000 hertz test tone, leaving only noise and distortion. SINAD is the ratio of the 2: signal plus noise plus distortion, divided by noise plus distortion. 12 decibels SINAD is the usual sensitivity reference.

params.title: Reading an analog RF wattmeter
params.formula: Error = ±5% of full scale (100 W) = ±5 W
steps: At 90 W: 5 W ÷ 90 W ≈ 6% of the reading
At 20 W: 5 W ÷ 20 W = 25% of the reading
params.answer: Most accurate in the upper one third of the dial

onScreen: Most accurate: upper one third of the dial
scenes.narration: An analog RF wattmeter gives its most accurate reading at the upper one third of the dial. Here's why. Its accuracy is a percentage of full scale. On a 100 watt scale with plus or minus 5 percent accuracy, the error is plus or minus 5 watts anywhere on the dial. At a 90 watt reading, 5 watts is only about 6 percent of the reading. At a 20 watt reading, the same 5 watts is 25 percent. So choose a scale that puts the needle in the upper one third.

params.title: Deviation meter and spectrum analyzer
labels: Deviation meter: measures carrier deviation in an FM transmitter
Spectrum analyzer: most likely used to measure spurious signals
Spurious signals show as separate spikes beside the carrier

onScreen: Spurious signals: spikes beside the carrier
scenes.narration: Last, 2 transmitter instruments. The purpose of a deviation meter is to measure the carrier deviation in an FM, or frequency modulation, transmitter: how far the carrier frequency swings as it is modulated, like the bunching and spreading in this FM signal. And the most likely reason to observe a transmitter's output with a spectrum analyzer is to measure spurious signals. On the analyzer, spurious signals show up as separate spikes beside the carrier.
